## Overview

Tool-call argument repair in the parser engine now keeps typed values for
untyped schema properties and rewrites arguments **in place**, so schema-aware
correction can never invalidate an already-streamed argument prefix. Streaming
correction is incremental: each delta rescans only the tail after the last
finalized member and survives ticks an argument extender streams, so long
streams no longer pay a full-document rewrite per tick. Fixes the
untyped-schema stringification reported in #47557
(typed-value half) and supersedes #47560.

## Claims

- Typed values emitted for untyped schema properties (JSON and K2
  `xml_typed`) are kept as-is instead of being stringified and re-coerced
  through a `json.dumps` round trip.
- Streamed tool-call arguments remain prefix-consistent under **any** model
  formatting: previously, a coerced or sanitized value in the middle of a
  partial object produced text that could not extend the already-streamed
  prefix, silently truncating the call (`startswith` failure in the flush).
- Streamed correction is incremental and composes with `arg_value_extender`.
  The per-slot cache resumes after the last top-level comma whose member is
  finalized and starts with a quoted key whenever that finalized prefix is
  unchanged — not only when the whole converter output is a prefix — and
  extender output advances the cache instead of invalidating it. The re-parsed
  tail must reproduce the text already emitted from that comma, including the
  extender's bytes; otherwise the delta falls back to a full pass. It never
  resumes past a structural give-up.
- Union handling is conjunctive where it decides whether a schema is untyped:
  an untyped `anyOf` branch no longer overrides a typed `oneOf`, and every
  `allOf` branch must be untyped. Declared types are still unioned across
  `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`.
- Value-preserving re-encodings stay verbatim: `5e3` under an integer schema,
  overflowing literals (`1e999`), and untyped-union literals are no longer
  rewritten to a different textual form of the same (or a wrong) value.
- K2 Horizon `xml_typed` calls honor the model's explicit `<arg_type>` tag
  when the property schema is untyped or resolves no type (an unresolved
  `$ref`), matching the missing-schema path.
- A property whose only constraint is an unresolved `$ref` (common in
  Pydantic-generated schemas, e.g. int-enum references) keeps the emitted
  type instead of being repaired toward string.
- Pathological nesting cannot crash a request. The argument rewriter and both
  schema walks share a 200-level bound: deeper argument nesting passes through
  verbatim, and a client-supplied schema nested past the cap is treated as
  unknown/constrained instead of raising `RecursionError`.
- A `false` schema contributes no type to a union and honors the caller's
  `fallback`.
- The schema-less fast path only parses when a **bare** `NaN`/`Infinity`
  token is present, not when that text merely occurs inside a string (e.g.
  `"banaNaNa"`).

## Validation

All new tests were verified to fail on the pre-fix tree for the reported
reason before the fix (representative output in the collapsible section).

<details>
<summary>Representative pre-fix failures (same tests, main worktree)</summary>

```text
# streamed prefix invalidation (the core streaming bug): a coerced middle
# value makes the corrected text unable to extend the streamed prefix, so
# the flush truncates the call and the coercion never appears at all
main streamed args : '{"count": "5", "note": "x'
expected (this PR) : '{"count": 5, "note": "x"}'

# bare NaN is streamed as-is: invalid JSON for strict clients
main (NaN case)    : '{"a":1,"x":NaN}'   expected: '{"a":1,"x":"NaN"}'

# exponent literal re-encoded under an integer schema (pre-fix on this branch)
E AssertionError: assert '{"n": 5000.0}' == '{"n": 5e3}'

# K2 xml_typed: untyped property drops the explicit <arg_type> tag
E AssertionError: assert {'query': 'x', 'limit': '5'} == {'query': 'x', 'limit': 5}

# deep argument nesting crashed the rewriter with an uncaught RecursionError
E RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded

# a deeply nested client schema crashed the schema walk on every call
E RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded

# $ref-only property stringified a correct int (pre-fix on this branch)
E AssertionError: assert {'level': '3'} == {'level': 3}

# K2 xml_typed: $ref-only property drops the explicit <arg_type> tag
E AssertionError: assert {'query': 'x', 'limit': '5'} == {'query': 'x', 'limit': 5}

# an extender tick or a re-serialized trailing member forced a full pass per tick
E AssertionError: 81 caches for 359 ticks
E assert None == ('"y", "c": ', False)

# a false schema branch injected a bogus string type into the union
E AssertionError: assert ['integer', 'string'] == ['integer']
```

</details>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_parser_engine.py \
    tests/parser/engine/test_granite.py tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py \
    tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py \
    tests/tool_parsers/test_k2_horizon_tool_parser.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/ tests/tool_parsers/ -q
pre-commit run --files <changed files>
```

Result: 673 tests in the five directly-affected files pass; the full
`tests/parser/` + `tests/tool_parsers/` run passes (8284 passed, 1 skipped,
30 xfailed), except known environmental errors (26 in this run: harmony
`TestAdjustRequest` needs a GPU; a gated HF repo such as
`meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` needs auth where it is not cached).
Pre-commit passes on all changed files.

Behavior was additionally probed against `main` directly (A/B on a detached
worktree): `main` truncates streamed calls whenever a middle value needs
correction and the model's formatting differs from `json.dumps` output
(compact/pretty/tab separators, exponent numbers, bare `NaN`); this branch
streams the complete corrected text in all six probed scenarios. A fuzz run
of 7000+ streaming simulations (random schemas, chunk sizes 1–7, NaN /
overflow / escape / unicode payloads) found zero prefix violations; a
differential fuzz of the incremental rewrite against the pre-incremental
implementation found 0/30000 divergences, and a differential fuzz of the
finalized-prefix resume against a fresh full pass (4,000 complete-document
sequences and 1,500 extender-driven streams) found zero divergences. Per-tick
argument deltas are byte-identical to the pre-change implementation for Qwen3
long-value and many-field streams. Nesting is parsed recursively but bounded
at 200 levels on both the document and schema sides.

Composition with #55743 (merged): the exact-integer fast path and the
value-gate here compose — a 20-digit integer under a `number` schema is now
both exact and kept verbatim; exponent forms under `integer` stay verbatim,
under `number` still normalize to `5000`-style integers.

Model evaluation is not applicable: the change is deterministic
post-generation coercion of tool-call arguments and does not alter
inference, sampling, or model output.

<details>
<summary>Perf measurements</summary>

End-to-end `_compute_arg_delta` A/B against `origin/main` (interleaved runs,
medians, same host, 4-character ticks). This measures the engine path, not
the isolated correction step:

| stream | main | this PR | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Granite, 60 short fields | 80.4 ms | 36.9 ms | **2.2x faster** |
| Granite, one 4 KB string | 1191.2 ms | 413.9 ms | **2.9x faster** |
| Qwen3, 60 short fields | 33.8 ms | 25.0 ms | **1.35x faster** |
| Qwen3, 200 int fields | 333.7 ms | 238.3 ms | **1.40x faster** |
| Qwen3, 200 string fields | 519.2 ms | 381.8 ms | **1.36x faster** |
| Qwen3, 4 KB last value | 3.88 ms | 3.93 ms | parity |

Incremental correction is a clear win for parsers whose converter passes the
argument text through verbatim (Granite, Inkling). Extender-based XML parsers
(Qwen3, GLM-4.x, Gemma4, MiMo, MiniMax M2) re-serialize their converter output
on every tick, so no tick extends the previous document; the cache now resumes
on the finalized prefix instead, and extender output advances the cache rather
than discarding it. A full pass remains the fallback when the finalized prefix
changes or a re-parsed tail does not reproduce the emitted text; its isolated
cost is unchanged (~1.5–1.8x main's C round trip), and the no-schema fast path
keeps schema-less calls at parity. Tool properties are looked up once when a
call's name is emitted and cached on its slot.

The isolated correction microbenchmark (`_ArgsRewriter` plus
`_safe_arg_prefix`, 2.2–2.9x on coercion-heavy payloads and 1.5x on the
107 KB string) measures that full-pass path with the incremental cache
bypassed. It is the worst case for parsers with neither an extender nor a
verbatim converter, not the engine path in the table above. Harness
available on request (kept out of the PR as a one-off A/B instrument).

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `_fix_arg_types` repaired argument types by round-tripping
the whole document: `json.loads` → recursive coercion → `json.dumps`. Two
defects followed. First, properties without a `type` extracted the
historical `["string"]` fallback, so an already-typed value (`5`, `true`, a
nested object) was stringified and then "repaired" back — losing structure
for containers and emitting the wrong type for scalars in the untyped-union
case. Second, the final `json.dumps` normalized separators (`", "`, `": "`)
and number forms, so the corrected text of a delta did not extend the text
already streamed for earlier deltas; the flush's `startswith` check then
silently dropped the remainder of the call whenever a middle value needed
correction and the model's formatting differed from `json.dumps` output.

**Fix.** `_ArgsRewriter` rewrites the argument text **in place**: only
complete value tokens that a property schema coerces, plus bare
`NaN`/`Infinity` literals, are replaced; every other byte — separators,
whitespace, number formats, escapes, key order — stays verbatim, so a
rewritten delta extends every earlier one by construction. `_fix_arg_types`
is the rewriter at EOF. For streaming, a per-slot `_StreamingArgs` cache
resumes the rewriter from the last finalized member instead of re-parsing the
whole accumulated document, carries the safe-prefix boundary and split-escape
state forward, and falls back to a full pass whenever the finalized prefix
changes or the re-parsed tail does not reproduce the text already emitted.

tick, so the gate is the finalized prefix, not the whole previous document;
bytes an argument extender streamed advance the cache instead of invalidating
it, and the tail check covers them. It never resumes past the first structural
give-up, because a tail scan from a different start could infer different
corrections than a full pass.

schemas short-circuit coercion) and a conjunctive `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`
reading of `extract_types_from_schema`, threaded with a `fallback` parameter:
coercion callers pass `[]` so both explicitly untyped and unresolved-`$ref`
schemas keep emitted values verbatim, while callers that need a concrete type
keep the string default. Both recursive schema walks share
`MAX_NESTING_DEPTH = 200` with the argument rewriter, so neither client input
can recurse to the interpreter limit. `false` schemas honor the fallback
instead of injecting a string type, and a value-equality gate keeps
re-encodings that do not change a literal's type or value verbatim.

comma/resume scanners) lives in `vllm/parser/engine/arg_rewrite.py`;
`parser_engine.py` keeps the engine proper and delegates the prefix scan.
This is a pure extraction with no behavior change, and it removes the
forward reference from `_StreamingArgs` into `ParserEngine`.

**Scope.** The change is engine-level because the repaired path is reachable
from every typed-value parser (Granite, Inkling, Kimi K2, DeepSeek DSML) and
was wrong for all of them; text-format parsers are unaffected. Untyped *raw
text* behavior (the open question in #47557) is deliberately unchanged, and
the Rust frontend's string-preservation tests still pin that direction.

**⚠ Behavior change / migration note.** Values for untyped properties that
are JSON containers are now delivered as structured JSON instead of a
JSON-text string: `{"payload": {"a": [1, 2]}}` instead of
`{"payload": "{\"a\": [1, 2]}"}`. Clients that re-parsed the string are
unaffected; clients that expected a string fail loudly at their own parse
boundary. Non-finite floats (`NaN`) under untyped properties are delivered
as their string form so the arguments stay valid JSON. Likewise, a bare
number under a `$ref`-only property is no longer repaired toward string

unresolved reference) — corrupting a correct int was judged worse than

non-finite literal under a typed number/integer property now keep the call
with the string form (`"NaN"`) instead of failing to serialize and dropping
the whole tool-call group; non-finite values have no valid JSON form, and
losing valid sibling calls was judged worse than a string-typed value.

Python half takes the coercion-guessing direction rejected here — the
text-path question remains open on #47557). Composes with the merged #55743
(exact integers). #57005 and #50933 touch the same files and should rebase
on top of this; #47643, #49318, #61410 are complementary.

+"""In-place rewriting and incremental correction of tool-call argument JSON.
+
+:class:`_ArgsRewriter` performs one full rewrite; :class:`_StreamingArgs`
+caches the result per tool-call slot and rewrites only the tail a new delta
+can change.  Both keep every byte they do not need to replace, so the emitted
+text is always a prefix of the final arguments.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+
+import regex as re
+
+from vllm.parser.utils import next_non_ws
+from vllm.tool_parsers.utils import (
+    MAX_NESTING_DEPTH,
+    coerce_to_schema_type,
+    coerce_typed_value,
+    is_escaped,
+    is_undeclared_string,
+    schema_coercion_types,
+    value_changed,
+)
+
+_NON_FINITE_LITERALS = ("NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity")
+_NUMBER_CHARS = frozenset("0123456789+-.eE")
+# Approximates a bare non-finite literal token: the lookarounds reject
+# identifiers ("banaNaNa") and quoted occurrences, but not a token inside a
+# longer string.  Fragments cannot be string-scanned, so callers that hold a
+# document use ``_document_has_non_finite_literal`` instead.
+_NON_FINITE_RE = re.compile(
+    r'(?<![\w"])(?:' + "|".join(_NON_FINITE_LITERALS) + r')(?![\w"])'
+)
+# Characters of a non-finite literal that can precede a delta boundary.
+_NON_FINITE_OVERLAP = max(map(len, _NON_FINITE_LITERALS)) - 1
+_JSON_STRING_RE = re.compile(r'"[^"\\]*(?:\\.[^"\\]*)*"', re.DOTALL)
+
+
+def _has_non_finite_literal(text: str) -> bool:
+    """Whether *text* may contain a bare non-finite literal.
+
+    Over-approximates inside strings, which is all a fragment permits: a
+    false positive only costs a structural pass, a false negative would miss
+    a rewrite.
+    """
+    # Cheap C-level pre-filter; only a text containing a candidate substring
+    # pays for the regex scan that rejects non-token occurrences.
+    if "NaN" not in text and "Infinity" not in text:
+        return False
+    return _NON_FINITE_RE.search(text) is not None
+
+
+def _document_has_non_finite_literal(text: str) -> bool:
+    """Whether the document *text* contains a bare non-finite literal.
+
+    Unlike :func:`_has_non_finite_literal`, text inside strings is ignored,
+    so an argument naming ``-Infinity`` does not disable the no-schema fast
+    path.  An unmatched quote opens the unterminated trailing string, whose
+    content cannot contain a bare token yet.
+    """
+    if not _has_non_finite_literal(text):
+        return False
+    outside = _JSON_STRING_RE.sub("", text)
+    quote = outside.find('"')
+    if quote != -1:
+        outside = outside[:quote]
+    return _NON_FINITE_RE.search(outside) is not None

+def _is_literal(literal: str) -> bool:
+    """Whether *literal* is a complete bare boolean, null, or number token."""
+    if literal in ("true", "false", "null"):
+        return True
+    if all(c in _NUMBER_CHARS for c in literal):
+        try:
+            float(literal)
+        except ValueError:
+            return False
+        return True
+    return False
+
+
+def _literal_changes_value(literal: str, coerced: object) -> bool:
+    """Whether coercing *literal* to *coerced* changes its value or type."""
+    try:
+        parsed = json.loads(literal)
+    except ValueError:
+        return True
+    return value_changed(parsed, coerced)

+class _ArgsRewriter:
+    """Rewrite tool-call argument JSON in place.
+
+    Only complete value tokens that a property schema coerces, plus
+    ``NaN``/``Infinity`` literals (invalid JSON), are replaced; every other
+    byte — separators, whitespace, number formats, escapes, key order — is
+    kept verbatim.  A rewritten token is final; a token still undelimited
+    may be rewritten once its delimiter arrives, but ``safe_arg_prefix``
+    never emits it before then, so streamed argument deltas stay
+    prefix-consistent however the model formats its JSON: the final
+    arguments are always the streamed text plus a suffix.  Re-serializing
+    with ``json.dumps`` instead would normalize separators and numbers,
+    breaking that prefix.  A truncated tail is passed through unchanged.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        text: str,
+        properties: dict | None,
+        *,
+        final: bool,
+        force_parse: bool = False,
+    ) -> None:
+        self._text = text
+        self._props = properties

+        # treated as still growing: it is only rewritten once delimited.
+        self._final = final
+        # Parse even when the identity fast path would apply, so streaming
+        # callers can learn where structural parsing stops (see ``stop``).
+        self._force_parse = force_parse
+        self._out: list[str] = []
+        # Schema id -> coercion types.  Every schema is reachable from
+        # ``self._props``, which the rewriter holds, so no live id is reused.
+        self._types_cache: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
+        # Offset where the first unparsable token made the rewriter copy the
+        # rest verbatim, or ``None`` if it parsed to the end.
+        self.stop: int | None = None
+
+    def rewrite(self) -> str:
+        text = self._text
+        if (
+            not self._props
+            and not self._force_parse
+            and not _document_has_non_finite_literal(text)
+        ):
+            # Without a property schema only non-finite literals are rewritten.
+            return text
+        i = self._skip_ws(0)
+        if i >= len(text) or text[i] != "{":
+            return text
+        j = self._object(i, self._props, 0)
+        if j < len(text):
+            # Text past the closed top-level object is copied verbatim; a
+            # tail scan must not resume inside it and correct it differently.
+            if self.stop is None:
+                self.stop = j
+            self._out.append(text[j:])
+        return "".join(self._out)
+
+    def _skip_ws(self, i: int) -> int:
+        j = next_non_ws(self._text, i)
+        if j > i:
+            self._out.append(self._text[i:j])
+        return j
+
+    def _scan_string(self, i: int) -> tuple[str | None, int] | None:
+        """Return ``(value, end)`` for the closed string at *i*, else None.
+
+        *value* is ``None`` when the string is closed but not valid JSON
+        (e.g. an invalid escape); callers copy it verbatim instead of
+        giving up on everything after it.
+        """
+        text = self._text
+        m = _JSON_STRING_RE.match(text, i)
+        if m is None:
+            return None
+        j = m.end()
+        if text.find("\\", i + 1, j) != -1:
+            try:
+                return json.loads(text[i:j]), j
+            except ValueError:
+                return None, j
+        return text[i + 1 : j - 1], j

+    def _truncated(self, i: int, *, give_up: bool = True) -> int:

+        # remainder verbatim, but only the former bounds incremental resuming.
+        if give_up and self.stop is None:
+            self.stop = i
+        self._out.append(self._text[i:])
+        return len(self._text)
+
+    def _delimited(self, j: int) -> bool:
+        k = next_non_ws(self._text, j)
+        return k < len(self._text) and self._text[k] in ",}]"
+
+    def _coercion_types(self, schema: dict) -> list[str]:
+        """Types a literal under *schema* coerces to; ``[]`` for none."""
+        cached = self._types_cache.get(id(schema))
+        if cached is not None:
+            return cached
+        types = schema_coercion_types(schema)
+        self._types_cache[id(schema)] = types
+        return types
+
+    def _next_member(self, i: int, closer: str) -> tuple[int, bool]:
+        """Copy the separator after a member; return ``(offset, closed)``."""
+        text, out = self._text, self._out

+        if i < len(text) and text[i] == ",":
+            out.append(",")
+            return self._skip_ws(i + 1), False

+            out.append(closer)
+            return i + 1, True
+        # Only a pending input is a wait; trailing whitespace after a
+        # complete member is not a structural give-up.
+        return self._truncated(i, give_up=i < len(text)), True
+
+    def _object(self, i: int, props: dict | None, depth: int) -> int:
+        text, out = self._text, self._out
+        out.append("{")
+        i = self._skip_ws(i + 1)
+        while True:
+            if i >= len(text):
+                return i
+            if text[i] == "}":
+                out.append("}")
+                return i + 1
+            scanned = self._scan_string(i) if text[i] == '"' else None
+            if scanned is None:
+                # A non-string key is a give-up; an unterminated one may close.
+                return self._truncated(i, give_up=text[i] != '"')
+            key, j = scanned
+            out.append(text[i:j])
+            i = self._skip_ws(j)
+            if i >= len(text) or text[i] != ":":
+                return self._truncated(i, give_up=i < len(text))
+            out.append(":")
+            i = self._skip_ws(i + 1)
+            i = self._value(i, props.get(key) if props else None, depth)
+            i, done = self._next_member(i, "}")
+            if done:
+                return i
+
+    def _array(self, i: int, items: dict | None, depth: int) -> int:
+        text, out = self._text, self._out
+        out.append("[")
+        i = self._skip_ws(i + 1)
+        while True:
+            if i >= len(text):
+                return i
+            if text[i] == "]":
+                out.append("]")
+                return i + 1
+            i = self._value(i, items, depth)
+            i, done = self._next_member(i, "]")
+            if done:
+                return i
+
+    def _value(self, i: int, schema: object, depth: int) -> int:
+        text, out = self._text, self._out
+        if i >= len(text):
+            return i
+        c = text[i]
+        if c in "{[":
+            if depth >= MAX_NESTING_DEPTH:
+                return self._truncated(i)
+            subkey = "properties" if c == "{" else "items"
+            nested = schema.get(subkey) if isinstance(schema, dict) else None
+            walk = self._object if c == "{" else self._array
+            return walk(i, nested if isinstance(nested, dict) else None, depth + 1)
+        if c == '"':
+            scanned = self._scan_string(i)
+            if scanned is None:
+                return self._truncated(i, give_up=False)
+            value, j = scanned
+            if value is not None and isinstance(schema, dict):
+                types = self._coercion_types(schema)
+                if types:
+                    coerced, changed = coerce_typed_value(value, schema, types=types)
+                    if changed:
+                        out.append(json.dumps(coerced, ensure_ascii=False))
+                        return j
+            out.append(text[i:j])
+            return j
+        return self._literal(i, schema)
+
+    def _literal(self, i: int, schema: object) -> int:
+        text, out = self._text, self._out
+        j = i
+        while j < len(text) and (text[j] in _NUMBER_CHARS or text[j].isalpha()):
+            j += 1
+        literal = text[i:j]
+        if not literal:
+            return self._truncated(i)
+        if literal in _NON_FINITE_LITERALS and (self._final or j < len(text)):
+            # Not valid JSON as a bare literal; the quoted string form is.
+            # A token at the end of the text may still grow, so wait for one
+            # more character; once it cannot, quote it even when the text
+            # that follows is malformed, since the final pass will too.
+            out.append(f'"{literal}"')
+            return j
+        if isinstance(schema, dict) and self._delimited(j):
+            types = self._coercion_types(schema)
+            if types and _is_literal(literal):
+                # Integral floats normalize (5.0 -> 5, 5e3 -> 5000), matching
+                # the parse-and-redump repair. A literal the declared types
+                # cannot hold exactly (5.5 under integer, 1e999) stays
+                # verbatim.
+                coerced = coerce_to_schema_type(literal, types)
+                dumped = json.dumps(coerced, ensure_ascii=False)
+                if (
+                    dumped != literal
+                    and _literal_changes_value(literal, coerced)
+                    and not is_undeclared_string(coerced, types)
+                ):
+                    out.append(dumped)
+                    return j
+        out.append(literal)
+        return j
